title: Collaborative Knowledge Graph
definition: A system that uses cryptographic hashes and IPLD to create a verifiable, interdisciplinary knowledge graph for collaborative research.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of it as a digital library that helps multiple people work together on research. It uses special codes to make sure the information is accurate and unchanged.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A collaborative knowledge graph is a graph database that leverages IPLD and cryptographic Content Identifiers (CIDs) for immutable, verifiable attribution in collaborative research. It enables schema-driven concept mapping, auditing, and local operation.
difficulty_levels.expert: A collaborative knowledge graph is a distributed system that combines the benefits of a graph database with the principles of content-addressed storage and cryptography. By using IPLD and CIDs, it creates a tamper-proof, verifiable representation of knowledge that can be used to study knowledge representation and scholarly communication. It also has practical applications in academic research, such as tracking contributions in collaborative projects. Furthermore, it serves as a novel application of content-addressing technology in academic contexts, opening up new possibilities for research and innovation.

extra_fields.insight: CADMIES-IPLD is a demonstration of how content-addressing technology can be used to create a verifiable, collaborative knowledge graph for research.
